summary: send-usdc is an instruction-only skill that tells the agent to run the unpinned npm package `npx awal@latest` (status, balance, send) to transfer USDC on Base to a 0x address or ENS name from the operator's authenticated wallet. It asks for no environment variables or private keys, but it needs node/npx, network access to the npm registry and the awal wallet backend, and Ethereum mainnet access for ENS resolution. Wallet login is by email through a separate `authenticate-wallet` skill that is not included. requires.env is empty and no metadata.openclaw block is declared. The frontmatter pre-approves send commands and allows model invocation, with no confirmation step.

findings.message: The skill runs `npx awal@latest send`, which downloads the newest version of the npm package `awal` at each run and executes it with authority over a funds-moving wallet, with no version pin or integrity check.
The skill card itself acknowledges that the mutable external wallet package `awal` may move funds and recommends pinning, but SKILL.md never pins it.
The skill moves USDC out of the operator's authenticated awal wallet; it never asks for a raw private key or seed, but it relies on a wallet credential or session held by the awal tool.

Authentication is by `awal auth login <email>`, and the actual login flow is delegated to an `authenticate-wallet` skill that is not part of this release, so credential handling cannot be reviewed here.
allowed-tools pre-approves `npx awal@latest send *` with a wildcard, and line 5 leaves model invocation enabled, so the agent can send funds to any recipient and amount without a separate approval.
The amount rule treats numbers with no decimal point or above 100 as atomic units, which contradicts the example `send 1` meaning $1.00 on line 45 and risks sending a wrong amount.
The skill card admits the artifact has no built-in transfer confirmation guidance, and SKILL.md has no step to confirm amount, recipient, resolved ENS address or chain before sending.

The command forms are inconsistent: `npx awal@latest awal status` and `npx awal balance` (no @latest) differ from the allowed-tools patterns on line 6, and bare `awal ...` on lines 74-75 assumes a global install.
The frontmatter has no metadata.openclaw block, so the dependency on node/npx and the awal package and the network access it needs are not declared.

ENS names are resolved through Ethereum mainnet, so the recipient name is sent to an RPC endpoint the skill does not name; the transfer goes to the awal backend and Base network, and the package comes from the npm registry.
